Lalremsiami: Damini, I know an apology can't undo it. I shouldn't have shown your private messages to the group. I'm truly sorry.
Damini: Thank you for saying that plainly. I do forgive you. I'm not certain trust will come back the way it was.
Lalremsiami: That's fair. I don't expect it back straight away.
Damini: I'd like to keep seeing you at Friday class. But I won't share personal things for now.
Lalremsiami: Okay. Whatever level you choose is fine.
Damini: I'll see how things go over the next few months. Not your words. What you do.
Lalremsiami: Understood. Thank you for not cutting me off.

qa.a: Lalremsiami showed the group Damini's private messages.

qa.q: What worries Damini even after forgiving Lalremsiami?
qa.a: Damini worries that trust may not come back the way it was.

qa.q: How does Damini decide how close to be?
qa.a: By watching Lalremsiami's actions over the next few months rather than words, keeping Friday-class contact but sharing nothing personal for now.

qa.q: How might Lalremsiami feel about Damini's decision?
qa.a: Lalremsiami seems accepting and grateful: 'Thank you for not cutting me off' shows relief along with acceptance of the limit.

grounding: Damini forgives a serious breach without full reconciliation and sets closeness by actions over time, not words or guilt.

passage:
Counselling note, week four. Elizabeth, 25.

Elizabeth came in holding her phone. Her friend Salma, who last year told Elizabeth's ex-boyfriend private things about her family, has now sent a long apology. Elizabeth read parts of it aloud. It was sincere. Elizabeth's hands were tight around the phone as she read.

"She says she's changed. I want to believe her. I also feel sick when I think of having coffee with her like before."

I asked whether forgiving Salma and being close to her again had to be the same thing. Elizabeth looked surprised. She said she could let go of the anger, and maybe had already begun to, but that trust would take time.

We discussed a middle path: replying kindly, accepting the apology, and seeing Salma in groups for a while rather than one-to-one. Elizabeth said this felt right, and her shoulders loosened for the first time in the session.

Next session: check how the reply went.

qa.q: What did Salma tell Elizabeth's ex-boyfriend?
qa.a: She told him private things about Elizabeth's family.

qa.q: What was Elizabeth feeling as she read the apology aloud?
qa.a: Elizabeth felt torn, wanting to believe Salma but still sick at the thought of being close like before.

qa.q: What middle path did Elizabeth choose, and why is it sensible?
qa.a: Accepting the apology kindly but seeing Salma in groups for a while, so trust can be rebuilt through actions over time.

qa.q: How might Salma feel waiting for Elizabeth's reply?
qa.a: Salma likely feels anxious and remorseful, hoping her long apology will be accepted.

grounding: A counsellor's note shows a young woman whose friend apologised for a serious breach, choosing to forgive without full reconciliation and let closeness depend on actions over time.

passage:
Tuesday, 11 p.m.

Nirmala finally apologised today. In the office pantry, cornered by the kettle, eyes red. "Ira, I'm sorry. I told Mehta sir you were interviewing elsewhere because I was jealous. It was horrible."

I believed her. That's the strange part. She meant every word.

And I still didn't know what to say. It was three months ago that Mehta sir took me off the Singapore project because of her. Three months of eating lunch alone.

What I said: "Thank you for saying it. I forgive you." I meant that too. I don't want to carry the anger anymore; it's exhausting.

What I didn't say: "Let's be friends like before." Because I don't know yet. Words are easy at a kettle.

So here's my plan. Friendly at work. Lunch together sometimes, if she wants. No secrets for a while. If she's still the person she says she is in six months, maybe more.

For tonight, lighter. A bit.

qa.q: What did Nirmala tell Mehta sir about Ira?
qa.a: She told him Ira was interviewing elsewhere.

qa.q: How did Ira feel after Nirmala's apology?
qa.a: Ira felt torn: believing the apology and forgiving her, but still unsure and cautious about trusting her again.

qa.q: How does Ira separate forgiveness from full reconciliation?
qa.a: Ira forgives Nirmala and lets go of the anger, but keeps closeness limited, with no secrets for a while, and lets Nirmala's actions over time decide more.

qa.q: What was the apology like for Nirmala?
qa.a: Nirmala was ashamed and emotional, with red eyes, admitting she acted out of jealousy.

grounding: A diary entry shows someone whose colleague and friend apologised for a serious breach, who forgives her while deciding closeness based on actions over time.
